summary: Admit an approval-bound Telegram single-message deletion through the tenant-scoped Social API and connector projection boundary.

impacts.evidence: The route resolves the local publication, social channel and active Telegram account in the authenticated organization/workspace scope before invoking the deleter.
The operation receipt stores only the normalized remote publication deletion acknowledgement and excludes credentials, raw provider response and unnecessary channel data.
OpenAPI adds DELETE /social/publications/{publication_id} with normalized confirmed-result/pending responses.
The operation adds no event contract and does not rewrite the local publication lifecycle.
The additive social.post.delete capability and generated delete method expose the existing connector delete port without changing prior publication contracts.
The normalized result uses the existing tenant-scoped operation receipt and requires no schema change.
Authentication, tenant resolution, permission, enabled capability, immutable receipt, fixed connector egress and bounded remote identity are independent gates.
Deletion is irreversible and write-sensitive; it requires a matching approved social.publication.delete request for the exact local publication.
The host records the approved, idempotent privileged mutation through the existing approval and operation receipt boundary.
The tenant-scoped operation receipt prevents duplicate calls and keeps pending or ambiguous provider outcomes available for reconciliation.
The adapter uses fixed Telegram connector egress and no caller-controlled destination crosses the host boundary; inbound webhooks remain out of scope.
Provider failures are bounded and mapped to the existing Social API error surface.
Disabling social.post.delete removes the admitted result, while provider deletion is irreversible and limited to approved disposable-message qualification.
Deterministic API, runtime admission, connector, OpenAPI, SDK and frontend checks cover the operation.
